description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary opacities.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior (AP) chest radiograph. The image shows bilateral pulmonary opacities, more pronounced in the mid and lower lung zones. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The bony structures, including the ribs and clavicles, are intact. The radiograph suggests a possible infectious or inflammatory process in the lungs.

description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary findings and medical device placement.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior chest radiograph showing the thorax. There are bilateral pulmonary opacities, more pronounced in the lower lung fields, suggesting possible consolidation or infiltrates. Medical devices, including ECG leads and a central venous catheter, are visible. The bony structures, including the ribs and spine, appear intact. The heart size is within normal limits, and there is no obvious pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

Case_12001/figure3.jpg.source_caption: CT of the head and neck, sagittal view.

description.short_caption: Sagittal CT of the head and neck showing soft tissue and bony structures.
description.detailed_description: This sagittal CT image of the head and neck demonstrates detailed visualization of the cranial vault, nasal cavity, oropharynx, cervical spine, and surrounding soft tissues. The image is in a bone window setting, highlighting the bony structures such as the skull, vertebrae, and mandible. The soft tissues of the neck, including the airway and pharyngeal structures, are also visible. No obvious abnormalities such as fractures, masses, or fluid collections are apparent in this image.
visible_findings: sagittal view of the skull and cervical spine
clear visualization of nasal cavity and oropharynx

description.short_caption: Gram stain of pleural fluid showing gram-positive bacilli and inflammatory cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of pleural fluid. Numerous gram-positive bacilli are visible, appearing as purple rod-shaped organisms. Additionally, there are scattered inflammatory cells, including neutrophils, which are indicative of an inflammatory or infectious process. The background is lightly stained, aiding in the visualization of cellular and bacterial elements.

Case_12001/figure5.jpg.source_caption: CT of the chest, post thoracentesis, mediastinal window.

description.short_caption: CT chest, mediastinal window, post-thoracentesis with residual air and fluid noted.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest, viewed in the mediastinal window, shows the heart centrally with surrounding lung fields. There is evidence of residual air in the pleural space, consistent with a pneumothorax, and fluid is visible in the pleural cavity, likely residual from the thoracentesis procedure. The image also demonstrates normal mediastinal structures and no obvious masses or lymphadenopathy.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the neck showing soft tissue structures.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the neck demonstrates soft tissue structures, including the airway, vascular structures, and cervical vertebrae. The image shows contrast-enhanced areas, suggesting the use of intravenous contrast. There is no obvious evidence of abscess, mass, or significant swelling in the visible soft tissues. The bony structures appear intact, and the airway is patent.

Case_12001/figure6.jpg.source_caption: CT of the chest, lung window.

description.short_caption: Axial CT of the chest in lung window showing bilateral pulmonary findings.
description.detailed_description: This axial CT image of the chest, viewed in the lung window, demonstrates bilateral pulmonary abnormalities. There are areas of ground-glass opacities and consolidations visible in both lungs, more prominent in the lower lobes. The mediastinum and central airways appear unremarkable. The image is de-identified and includes standard CT imaging markers.

description.short_caption: Gram stain of neck aspirate showing gram-positive rods and inflammatory cells.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of a neck aspirate. Numerous gram-positive rods are visible, appearing as purple, rod-shaped structures. There are also abundant inflammatory cells, including neutrophils, with pink cytoplasm and multilobed nuclei. The background contains amorphous material, likely necrotic debris. The findings suggest a bacterial infection, possibly involving anaerobic or facultative anaerobic organisms.

Case_12001/figure7.jpg.source_caption: CT of the head and neck, with arrows showing air in the prevertebral space.

description.short_caption: CT of the head and neck showing air in the prevertebral space.
description.detailed_description: This sagittal CT image of the head and neck demonstrates abnormal air in the prevertebral space, indicated by arrows. The air appears as dark, radiolucent areas anterior to the cervical spine. The surrounding soft tissue structures and bony anatomy are well visualized. This finding is suggestive of a possible infection or trauma leading to gas formation or introduction into the prevertebral space.
visible_findings: normal bony anatomy of the cervical spine
soft tissue structures of the neck
